insights.subtitle: How your book is moving, and where the work is.
insights.empty_desc: Insights fills in as you add policies. Check your first policy and this page starts showing renewals, product mix and where your weak covers are.
insights.renewals_desc: Policies reaching their expiry date. Plan your calls around the tall months.
insights.mix_desc: Share of {{count}} policies. One colour, because a product type is not a warning.
insights.checks_desc_one: Across the {{count}} policy that carries a health check score. Other lines are data entry and are not scored.
insights.checks_desc_many: Across the {{count}} policies that carry a health check score. Other lines are data entry and are not scored.
insights.note_body: Every figure above is counted from the policies in your book right now.
insights.note_unknown_one: {{count}} policy has no expiry date recorded, so it is left out of the renewal figures rather than guessed at.
insights.note_unknown_many: {{count}} policies have no expiry date recorded, so they are left out of the renewal figures rather than guessed at.
insights.note_not_shown: Premium under management and lapse rate are deliberately not shown: we do not store a premium on a checked policy, and a lapse is not something the system can tell apart from a renewal written elsewhere. Showing either would mean inventing it.

pv.act_lapsed_blurb: The premiums stopped, so the policy is reduced paid-up: the values shown are what is actually left, not what it would have been worth. It can be brought back to full benefit by paying the arrears, but only until the revival window closes.
pv.act_overdue_blurb: The premium is past its grace period but the policy has not gone paid-up yet, so the benefits below still stand. Call before it does.
pv.act_maturing_blurb: Money is about to reach the customer. Call before someone else does.
pv.act_jumps_blurb: The surrender value rises noticeably at the next anniversary. Tell them to wait.
pv.act_underwater_blurb: Past halfway and the surrender value is still under the premiums paid. Normal for these products early on, worth a conversation this late.
pv.act_steady_blurb: Surrenderable today, above what has been paid in.
pv.act_locked_blurb: Nothing is payable yet. No action available.
pv.act_none_blurb: No surrender value at any point. Nothing to track.
pv.load_failed: Could not work out the policy values.
pv.title: Surrender values
pv.subtitle: What every life policy in your book is worth if the customer stopped today, what it would lend them instead, and what a lapsed one costs to bring back. Worked out from the policy documents by arithmetic, not estimated.
pv.c_borrow_sub: Raised without ending a single policy
pv.c_maturing_sub: Money about to reach the customer
pv.c_reviving_sub: Lapsed, or a premium past its grace period
pv.empty_all: No life or term policies with enough detail yet. Upload one, or fill in the premium, term and sum assured on an existing policy.
pv.footnote: * Held in the discontinued fund: the amount shown is what is released when the lock-in ends, not what is payable now. Every value is worked out from the policy document each time this page loads, so they move with the anniversary on their own. What a policy will lend is its own loan percentage applied to that day's surrender value; open a policy to see or correct it. Loan and revival interest rates stay blank until the reference G-Sec yield is set on the policy, because a rate quoted from a guess is one a customer would be told.
pv.headline_english: The one-line notes under each action are in English.

pvc.need_many: To work out the surrender value and maturity benefit we still need these fields filled in above:
pvc.nothing_guessed: Nothing is guessed here. Without these the numbers would be made up, so we show nothing instead.
pvc.v_term_title: Nothing comes back. That is what this policy is.
pvc.v_term_body: This is term cover. There is no surrender value at any point and no maturity benefit, so if the customer stops paying or outlives the policy they receive nothing. What they are buying is {{cover}} of cover, for {{total}} of premiums in total.
pvc.v_rop_title: All {{total}} of the premiums come back at the end.
pvc.v_rop_title_ret: All {{total}} of the premiums come back at the end, a return of {{ret}} a year.
pvc.v_rop_body: Stop earlier and only the guaranteed surrender value is paid, which stays below the premiums paid until close to the end of the term.
pvc.v_mb_title: {{payouts}} paid out along the way, plus {{maturity}} at maturity.
pvc.v_mb_title_ret: {{payouts}} paid out along the way, plus {{maturity}} at maturity, a return of {{ret}} a year.
pvc.v_mb_body: On {{total}} of premiums, the customer receives {{received}} in total. The regular payouts are money already in their hands, so they count towards the return. The cover and the maturity amount are separate figures, and neither is derived from the other.
pvc.v_end_title: About {{maturity}} at maturity, on {{total}} of premiums.
pvc.v_end_title_ret: About {{maturity}} at maturity, on {{total}} of premiums, a return of {{ret}} a year.
pvc.v_end_body: Surrender before the end pays the higher of the guaranteed value and the paid-up value, both well below the premiums paid for most of the term.
pvc.v_ulip_body: For the first {{years}} policy years nothing can be paid out. On surrender the fund moves to the discontinued fund, earns {{rate}}% a year and reaches the customer only after that date.
pvc.anchored: Anchored to the statement: {{value}} at policy year {{year}}. Later years are projected forward from that real figure.
pvc.modelled: No fund value from a statement, so this whole curve is modelled from the charge table. It is not the customer's actual fund. Add the fund value and the statement date above to fix that.
pvc.matches: Matches the illustration in the policy document ({{amount}} at maturity).
pvc.differs: The document's own illustration says {{doc}} at maturity. This works out to {{ours}}, a difference of {{diff}}%. Check the charges below against the policy wording.
pvc.plan_type_hint: This decides the whole calculation. If it is wrong, correct it here and everything below updates.
pvc.cover_family: Cover for the family, same years
pvc.scrub: Policy year {{year}} of {{term}}. Drag to move through the policy.
pvc.scrub_age: Policy year {{year}} of {{term}}, age {{age}}. Drag to move through the policy.
pvc.k_received_desc: Paid out along the way. They keep this whatever they decide next.
pvc.nothing_this_year: Nothing comes back in this year.
pvc.a_year_paid: A year, on the money actually paid in.
pvc.xirr_note: XIRR, using the real dates of each payment. Compare with a fixed deposit.
pvc.annual_note: Annual periods; no start date to date the payments.
pvc.cover_stops: Cover stops if the policy is surrendered.
pvc.cover_while: Cover while the policy is in force.
pvc.rpu_desc: Premiums stopped after {{paid}} of the {{ppt}} years payable, so every figure above is {{pct}}% of what this policy would otherwise be worth. Reviving it puts them back to full.
pvc.borrow_desc: Up to {{pct}}% of the surrender value, borrowed against the policy. The cover stays alive and so does the plan.
pvc.loan_rate: Interest {{rate}}% a year, fixed for the life of the loan.
pvc.loan_drawn: {{drawn}} already drawn, so {{left}} is left today.
pvc.forecloses: The loan has passed {{pct}}% of the surrender value. The policy can be foreclosed.
pvc.revival_rate: Interest charged at {{rate}}% a year on each arrear from its due date.
pvc.window_closed_on: The window closed on {{date}}. This policy can no longer be revived.
pvc.window_end: the end of the revival window
pvc.charges_desc: These come from the policy wording where it states them. Anything marked "assumed" is a standard value we applied so the schedule could be drawn. Set it from the customer's document and the numbers become exact.
pvc.how_desc: Every figure is arithmetic on the fields read from the document and the charges above. Nothing is estimated, and the same document always gives the same numbers.
pvc.how_return: · Return = the rate at which the premiums actually paid, year by year, grow into the payout (XIRR, discounted by the real dates). A plain average over total premiums would overstate it, because a premium paid late has not been invested for the whole term.
pvc.steps_english: The step-by-step working below is in English.
pvc.p_grossReturnPct: Assumed growth before charges (% a year)
pvc.p_adminEscalationPct: Administration charge rises by (% a year)
pvc.p_adminCapMonthly: Administration charge capped at (₹ a month)
pvc.p_deathBenefitFloorPct: Death benefit floor (% of premiums paid)
pvc.p_ssvSpreadBps: Special surrender value discount spread (bps over G-Sec)
pvc.p_foreclosureAtPct: Policy forecloses when loan reaches (% of surrender value)
pvc.p_revivalWindowYears: Revival allowed within (years of first unpaid premium)
pvc.p_outstandingLoan: Loan already taken against this policy (₹)
